Why checkout retries amplified a gateway outage

resolved

A 19-minute configuration error became a 47-minute customer impact because retries shared one synchronized schedule.

Impact

Sample incident data: 8.4% of checkout attempts failed between 14:02 and 14:49 UTC. The gateway configuration was corrected at 14:21, but synchronized client retries kept request volume above the safe recovery threshold.

Chronology

  1. Error threshold crossed14:02

    On-call paged after gateway rejections exceeded 5%.

  2. Configuration reverted14:21

    New requests began succeeding, but retry cohorts remained synchronized.

  3. Traffic recovered14:49

    Queue depth returned below the autoscaling threshold.

Causal chain

The initiating cause was a gateway config requiring a header that clients did not send. The duration cause was deterministic retry timing: clients that failed together retried together, preventing a smooth recovery.

Findings

  1. High

    Retries had no jitter

    Evidence. All clients used fixed delays of 1, 2, and 4 seconds.

    Consequence. Each recovery attempt produced another coordinated load spike.

    Action. Use full jitter and cap aggregate retry volume.

  2. Medium

    The config rollout lacked a compatibility check

    Evidence. Staging did not include the oldest supported client.

    Action. Add the compatibility case to the owning gateway gate.

Prevention

Ship jittered retries and one compatibility gate before the next gateway configuration change. Measure recovery load separately from initial failures so the alert explains both the trigger and the amplifier.
